_comment: Runtime guard, and the machine-readable half of a record kept in
The corpus is defined in registry.py as 24 datasets. This file exists
because scripts/run_study.py discovers datasets by globbing data/cache/,
so a .npz left over from characterisation would otherwise be picked up and
run even though it is not part of the corpus. Listing it here keeps the
runner in agreement with the corpus definition.
Nothing here was ever run: no shard exists for any dataset in this list,
so no result could have influenced its being set aside. A dataset dropped
AFTER its results were seen would not belong here -- that is a selection
effect, and it would have to be disclosed. Units merely too expensive to
run are passed to run_study.py --skip and reported as missing coverage.

datasets.wine_quality: Not adopted into the corpus: UCI id 186 serves red and white wine as one file, so the design matrix pools two chemically distinct populations and fails the single-population inclusion criterion. Never run; no shard exists.
